newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 5.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* United Parcel Service customers struggled to cope with the first day of a strike by the company's Teamsters union, while UPS rivals benefited from a huge pickup in business.
* Teamster President Carey, facing strong opposition within the union and alleged fund-raising abuses in his re-election campaign, needs a victory against UPS.
* News Corp plans a $250 million charge to restructure HaperCollins, which includes the shedding of some 420 jobs.
* Columbia/HCA named Jack Bovender president and chief operating officer.
* Mental-health benefits can be capped under group-disability plans without violating the Americans with Disabilities Act, an appeals court in Cincinnati ruled.
* General Motors said it will buy back $2.5 billion of its shares.
* Intel Corp is revamping its cooperative-ad program with customers in a way that may boost overall ad spending on the Internet 40.0 percent.
* CoreStates said its president Rosemarie Greco resigned for personal reasons.
* APL plans a new shipping service between Houston and Latin America.
* Medtronic won an FDA approval for a brain implant that helps tremor patients supress involuntary shaking in their hands and arms.
* The Dow Jones Industrials rose 4.41 to 8189.45, while bond prices fell and the dollar gained.
* Thailand's cabinet is expected to approve an IMF-negotiated recovery plan.
* Investors have been pulling money out of Asia mutual funds amid uncertainties sparked by the Thai crisis.
* Yamaichi Securities is facing legal woes that could drive it into the arms of a suitor.
* British Air posted a 47.0 percent rise in quarterly earnings, although its shares fell in London after the company said its losses from a labor dispute may total $203.8 million.
* Goldman, Sachs & Co held talks nearly two years ago with Salomon Inc about merging the two companies and becoming public in the process.
* The sharp rises in Treasury yields during the past two trading days may help spur demand for the Treasury's third-quarter refunding package sales this week.
